clue.text: Baddy and goody have a share — it goes to show!

parts.note: a demon is a wicked being
ST is the abbreviation for saint, the ultimate good person
a ration is an allotted portion

explanation.surface: Villain and hero split the takings, which just goes to prove something.
explanation.walkthrough: DEMON + ST + RATION. ST for saint is a standard crossword goody.
explanation.definitionFit: A demonstration is something put on to show people how a thing works or what is true.

clue.text: Trace exit — unusual way to get out

indicators.note: an unusual version of the words is an irregular arrangement of their letters

parts.note: the two words taken letter for letter

explanation.surface: Following an exit by an odd route is how to escape.
explanation.definitionFit: To extricate is to free oneself or something from a tangle or difficulty, i.e. to escape it.

clue.text: Vegetable for one caught up in forbidding situation

indicators.note: in a down entry, going up means the letters are read from bottom to top
something caught is held inside, so one letter sits within the others

parts.note: a no-no is a forbidden thing
I is the Roman numeral one

explanation.surface: Someone is trapped in a prohibited spot and a vegetable is involved.
explanation.walkthrough: A no-no is something forbidden; in a down entry 'up' turns it round before the one is caught inside.
explanation.definitionFit: The onion is a pungent bulb eaten as a common kitchen vegetable.

clue.text: Hitler's uncontrolled progress?

indicators.note: letters that are uncontrolled run wild and fall out of order

parts.note: the name with its possessive S, letter for letter

explanation.surface: A question about the dictator's unchecked advance across Europe.
explanation.walkthrough: The question mark flags that a slither is a rather unusual kind of progress, sliding rather than marching.
explanation.definitionFit: A slither is a sliding, snakelike movement along the ground, one way of making headway.

clue.text: It's binding on official intelligence

parts.note: surface reading: some rule that official spies must obey
setter's reading: the coloured ribbon literally tied round bundles of government papers

explanation.walkthrough: Official documents were once tied with a coloured ribbon, which gave its name to bureaucratic obstruction.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase means excessive bureaucratic rules, named after the ribbon used to tie up official documents.

clue.text: Put in solution as instructed — no second turn

indicators.note: giving the letters a turn churns them into a new order
no second says the abbreviation for second is dropped from the word

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A lab assistant dissolves something as directed, without a second stir.
explanation.walkthrough: S (second) is taken out of INSTRUCTED and the remaining letters are rearranged.
explanation.definitionFit: A tincture is a medicine dissolved in alcohol, so something tinctured has been steeped or infused in a liquid.

clue.text: Some children, women and dogs upset the proprietor

indicators.note: in a down entry, upset means tipped over so the run reads bottom to top
some of the words means only a run of their letters is used

parts.note: a run straddling the end of children and the start of women

explanation.surface: Kids, wives and pets cause trouble for the landlord.
explanation.walkthrough: The letters sit in childRENWOmen and read upwards; 'and dogs' is surface dressing.
explanation.definitionFit: An owner is the person who possesses something, which is what a proprietor is.

clue.text: Promise shown by a workman — there's the nub

parts.note: an operative is a factory worker
to give your word is to promise

explanation.surface: A labourer shows promise, and that's the crux of it.
explanation.walkthrough: The pieces appear in the clue in the reverse of answer order.
explanation.definitionFit: The operative word is the most significant one in a phrase, its key point or crux.

clue.text: One bears with dramatic bearing

parts.note: the stage is the world of drama
a person's bearing is their posture or carriage

explanation.surface: Someone tolerates another who has a theatrical manner.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bears' looks like enduring; here it is carrying passengers.
explanation.definitionFit: A stage carriage is a stagecoach or public vehicle that carries passengers along a route.

clue.text: Tripe, if turned out by journalist when stoned

indicators.note: something turned out is tipped and emptied, so its letters land in a new order

parts.note: the two words taken letter for letter
ED is short for editor

explanation.surface: Rubbish written by a reporter who was high at the time.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Stoned' suggests drugs; it means turned to stone.
explanation.definitionFit: Petrified literally means changed into stone, which is a punning sense of stoned.

clue.text: Set of nine or ten on reflection

indicators.note: a reflection in a mirror shows things back to front

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: Musing on whether a group has nine members or ten.
explanation.definitionFit: A nonet is a group of nine, especially nine musicians or a piece written for them.

clue.text: Rule of restraint without force

indicators.note: without in its old sense of outside, so one piece wraps round the other

parts.note: a rein is a strap that holds back a horse
G is the symbol for gravitational force, as in g-force

explanation.surface: A principle of self-control that needs no coercion.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Without' looks like lacking; it means outside, so REIN goes round G.
explanation.definitionFit: A reign is a monarch's period of rule or sovereignty.

clue.text: It may go down before a fire

definitions.text: It may go down before a fire

parts.words: It may go down before a fire
parts.note: surface reading: something such as a building or ship lost before a blaze breaks out
setter's reading: a mat laid on the floor in front of a fireplace

explanation.walkthrough: 'Go down' suggests sinking or collapsing; here it means being laid on the floor, and 'before' means in front of.
explanation.definitionFit: This mat is laid on the floor directly in front of a domestic fireplace.

clue.text: Tarmac damaged by first road vehicle

indicators.note: a damaged surface is broken up, so its letters are knocked out of order

parts.note: taken as written

indicators.note: first asks for only the opening letter of the next word

parts.note: the opening letter of road

explanation.surface: A road surface wrecked by the earliest motor vehicle.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Road vehicle' reads as one phrase, but road only lends its first letter.
explanation.definitionFit: A tramcar is a passenger vehicle running on rails in the street.

clue.text: Happy little girl and boy, about 10

indicators.note: the two names go about, that is round, the number

parts.note: Con is a pet form of Constance
the number in words
Ted is a short form of Edward

explanation.surface: A cheerful pair of youngsters, around ten years old.
explanation.walkthrough: 'About 10' looks like an age, but 'about' tells the two short names to stand either side of the number.
explanation.definitionFit: Contented means satisfied and at ease, a close synonym of happy.

clue.text: Not even little by little, a traitor infiltrated

indicators.note: an infiltrator slips inside an organisation, so one piece goes within another

parts.note: Eric, or Little by Little is a Victorian school story by F.W. Farrar
a rat is someone who betrays their side

explanation.surface: Bit by bit a turncoat worked his way into the organisation.
explanation.walkthrough: ER(RAT)IC. 'Little by little' looks like an adverb; it is the subtitle of a once-famous novel, standing for its title.
explanation.definitionFit: Erratic means irregular and unpredictable, the opposite of steady or uniform.

clue.text: Chatty chess champion, a girl about 4

parts.note: Mikhail Tal was world chess champion in 1960

indicators.note: about means around, so the girl's name wraps round the number

parts.note: a girl's name
Roman numeral four

explanation.surface: A talkative young chess prodigy, a girl of about four.
explanation.walkthrough: TAL + KAT(IV)E.
explanation.definitionFit: Talkative describes someone fond of talking, exactly what chatty means.

clue.text: Native unrest starting massacre in the Far East

definitions.note: the answer is a country located there

indicators.note: unrest is disturbance, so the letters are stirred up

parts.note: taken as written

indicators.note: starting points to the opening letter of the following word

parts.note: the opening letter of massacre

explanation.surface: Local uprisings beginning with a massacre somewhere in East Asia.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition names a place by where it lies rather than by a synonym.
explanation.definitionFit: Vietnam is a country in South-East Asia, part of the region called the Far East.

clue.text: A short time down and age going up — time on the tower

parts.note: MIN is short for minute

indicators.note: in a down entry, going up means the word is read from bottom to top

parts.note: an era is an age
T is the abbreviation for time

explanation.surface: Clock faces and ages on a church tower.
explanation.walkthrough: MIN is written first, down the grid, then ERA reversed, then T at the foot.
explanation.definitionFit: A minaret is the slender tower of a mosque from which the call to prayer is made.

clue.text: Field doctor treated bowman

indicators.note: something treated has been processed and altered, so the letters are rearranged

parts.note: taken as written
DR is the abbreviation for doctor

explanation.surface: A medic at the front patches up a wounded archer.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bowman' suggests an archer; this bow is drawn across strings.
explanation.definitionFit: A fiddler plays the violin with a bow, so is a whimsical kind of bowman.

clue.text: Limb singled out for elegance — not half!

indicators.note: not half says that half of the word's letters are removed

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written, before trimming

explanation.surface: A leg picked out for its grace, and how!
explanation.walkthrough: ELEGANCE has eight letters, and dropping the last four leaves ELEG. 'Not half!' also reads as the British exclamation meaning 'very much so'.
explanation.definitionFit: A foreleg is one of the front legs of an animal, so it is a limb.

clue.text: Perhaps Californian Guardian is more rigorous

parts.note: the newspaper speaks of itself in the editorial we
sterner means stricter

explanation.surface: The Guardian is tougher than some American from the West Coast.
explanation.walkthrough: The clue appeared in The Guardian, whose editorial voice is 'we'. 'Perhaps' marks a Californian as one example.
explanation.definitionFit: A Californian lives in the western United States, so is one example of a westerner.

clue.text: Least fresh?

indicators.note: a fresh version of a word is a new arrangement of its letters

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue does double duty: read straight it defines the answer, and 'fresh' also tells you to rework the word before it.
explanation.definitionFit: Stale food has lost its freshness, so it is the least fresh of all.

clue.text: Shade said to facilitate vehicular access

indicators.note: said means the words are spoken, and we go by their sound

parts.note: a car key is what lets you into a vehicle

explanation.surface: A colour that is claimed to make it easier to get into cars.
explanation.walkthrough: This works with the British pronunciation, roughly 'kar-kee'.
explanation.definitionFit: Khaki is a dull yellowish-brown colour, famous from military uniforms.

clue.text: Serpent — old craft put up with it

indicators.note: in a down entry, put up means lifted so it reads bottom to top

parts.note: Noah's ark is the most ancient boat
taken as written

explanation.surface: A snake in an ancient boat that had to be tolerated.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Put up with' looks like tolerate; it splits into the reversal signal and a link.
explanation.definitionFit: The krait is a highly venomous snake found in South and South-East Asia.

clue.text: Joint feature of Zoroastrian ritual?

indicators.note: a feature of something is a part within it, so the letters lie inside the words

parts.note: a run inside the first of these words

explanation.surface: Wondering whether a shared spliff belongs in an ancient Persian ceremony.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Joint' suggests a cannabis cigarette or a body part; it is a cut of meat for the oven.
explanation.definitionFit: A roast is a joint of meat cooked in the oven, so the two words name the same thing.

clue.text: Authorising publication about falsehood

parts.note: re means concerning
leasing is an archaic word for lying

explanation.surface: Allowing something to be printed on a matter of lies.
explanation.walkthrough: Leasing in the sense of lying survives in Scots law and the Bible.
explanation.definitionFit: Releasing a film, record or document means letting it be issued to the public.

clue.text: Summit meeting? It could go with a bang!

definitions.meaning: first meaning: a private consultation, the leaders conferring closely

definitions.text: It could go with a bang!
definitions.meaning: second meaning: what you might knock together with a thump

explanation.walkthrough: A summit is a head, so a meeting of summits is heads coming together, and knocking them together makes a bang.
explanation.definitionFit: To put your heads together means to confer closely, and heads knocked together literally collide noisily.
